specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:1:# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:3:**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:9:**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:17:- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:25:**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:98:4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:112:- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md:129:- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.

content.text:
Clean analysis, all tests pass.

## Summary

Root cause: when the SSE stream's very first (or only) item is a `Left(failure)` — before any `token` event ever arrives — `ChatBloc` marks the assistant bubble `failed` with empty content immediately (`lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_bloc.dart`, `_applyFailure`). This is exactly what shows as "Falha ao gerar resposta" with no partial text, on a 200 response, with nothing thrown at the Dio layer (so no exception in the log) — the failure comes from a frame/event the client itself interprets as terminal, while the backend keeps generating in the background and finishes shortly after, which is why reopening the conversation shows the complete answer. "Already-asked" content streams fine because it hits a path (likely cached/faster) that doesn't trigger this early-failure window.

Fix: `ChatBloc._consumeTurn` now does a one-shot reconciliation after the stream ends — only when the turn's bubble is `failed` with empty content — by refetching `listMessages(sessionId)` and matching the persisted assistant message by `seq`. If the backend already completed and persisted the answer, the failed bubble is replaced with it instead of leaving a false failure; if nothing is there yet, it stays failed exactly as before (no phantom recovery). A genuine failure with partial tokens (existing FR-005 behavior) is untouched.

Added two tests (`#8b`, `#8c`) covering both outcomes, and verified the whole [chat_bloc.dart](lib/features/chat/presentation/bloc/chat_bloc.dart) change against the full chat test suite (60 tests) and `flutter analyze` — all clean.

Note: I couldn't inspect the backend (not in this repo, and the original spec explicitly says not to touch it), so I can't confirm *why* the stream sends that early failure for novel questions specifically — only that the client now recovers gracefully when it does. If this keeps happening, it may be worth checking backend/edge-function logs for what's actually erroring during RAG retrieval on first-seen questions.

content.text:
## Summary

Root cause: the backend sends `createdAt` as UTC ISO-8601 timestamps (`Z` suffix), which `DateTime.parse` turns into a `DateTime` with `isUtc: true`. `ChatMessageBubble`'s timestamp line read `message.createdAt.hour`/`.minute` straight off that UTC instant via `TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(message.createdAt)`, with no `.toLocal()` conversion — so a message loaded from `listMessages` (history reopen) displayed its raw UTC hour instead of the wall-clock time. The sibling side-menu code ([app_drawer.dart:187](lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart#L187)) already converts with `.toLocal()` before formatting — the bubble was just missing that same step. Messages from the live session read correctly because the user bubble keeps its original client-side `DateTime.now()` (already local) and never gets overwritten.

Fix: [chat_message_bubble.dart:86](lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_message_bubble.dart#L86) now calls `message.createdAt.toLocal()` before formatting, matching the existing convention. Added a regression test that builds a message with a `DateTime.utc(...)` timestamp and asserts the rendered label matches `TimeOfDay.fromDateTime(utc.toLocal())` rather than the raw UTC value. Full chat suite (61 tests) and `flutter analyze` are clean.

INTERVENÇÃO [correção|S2|prd]: Expected: Home chat screen matching the prototype. Actual: (1) the prototype shows each message time below the bubble, small, gray and monospaced; the app shows it inside the bubble, in the regular font and larger. (2) In the failure state the prototype shows a small red text below the bubble, in place of the time; the app shows it inside the bubble, larger, making the bubble taller with empty space above the text. (3) The prototype send icon is an outlined paper plane; the app shows a filled arrow. Where: Home chat screen (Tela 1). Error: none, visual differences

content.text:
All 416 tests pass across the full project.

## Summary

Three visual deviations from the prototype, all in [chat_message_bubble.dart](lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_message_bubble.dart) and [chat_composer.dart](lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_composer.dart):

1. **Timestamp placement/style** — moved the time label out of the bubble's padded content and into a `Padding` below the bubble `Container`, inside a `Column`. Switched its style from `textLabelMd` (regular Karla) to `textMonoCaption` (IBM Plex Mono, 12px) per the design tokens' own spec for "technical metadata (timestamps...)".
2. **Failure text placement/style** — same relocation, below the bubble in place of where the timestamp would sit, same `textMonoCaption` style but in `colorError`. Since it's no longer constrained inside the bubble's padding, it no longer inflates the bubble's height.
3. **Send icon** — `Icons.send` (filled arrow) → `Icons.send_outlined` (outlined paper plane), matching the outlined-Material-icon convention this app already uses elsewhere to stand in for the prototype's Phosphor "Regular" style icons (e.g. `camera_alt_outlined`, `mic_none`).

Also restored the vertical gap between consecutive message bubbles (previously carried by the bubble's own margin, now on the wrapping `Padding`) so removing the timestamp from inside the bubble didn't collapse message spacing. Updated `chat_composer_test.dart`'s icon lookups to match the new icon. Full suite (416 tests) and `flutter analyze` are clean.

docs/input/requirements.md:12:Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
docs/input/requirements.md:24:Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
docs/input/requirements.md:38:Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
docs/input/requirements.md:42:- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
docs/input/requirements.md:45:Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
docs/input/requirements.md:50:- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
docs/input/requirements.md:55:A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
docs/input/requirements.md:82:- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
docs/input/requirements.md:105:| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
docs/input/requirements.md:112:RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
docs/input/requirements.md:168:**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

## Summary

Five visual deviations fixed in [app_drawer.dart](lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart):

1. **Avatar + name header** — the app had no `name` field anywhere (`Account` only has `id`/`email`, and the only `displayName` in the backend's API lives behind a settings-update endpoint from a later, not-yet-built unit). Per your direction to use judgment: I added `SecureTokenStorage.readAccountEmail()`, which decodes the `email` claim straight out of the already-stored access token's JWT payload — no new network call, no fabricated data. The drawer now shows a `colorPrimary` initials circle + a name derived from the email's local-part (e.g. `wagner.duarte@...` → "WD" / "Wagner Duarte"), replacing the old "Cerne" title block, with the divider still below it.
2. **"CONVERSAS" label** moved above the "Novo Chat" button (it was below).
3. **"Novo Chat"** is now a full-width `ElevatedButton.icon` (the theme's filled dark-green/`colorOnPrimary` style — already used everywhere else in the app) with a plus icon, replacing the plain `ListTile`.
4. **Relative timestamps** — added `ChatSessionTimestampFormatter` (today → `HH:mm`, last 6 days → weekday abbreviation + time, older → `DD mon`), replacing the old fixed `DD/MM HH:mm` for every session.
5. **Icons** added to "Meus Registros" (`menu_book_outlined`) and "Configurações" (`settings_outlined`).

Not implemented: **"Planos de Ação"** — it's explicitly marked `[ext]` (extension, not implemented) in the prototype extract, and RF04's own spec says not to build later-unit/extension features, so I left it out rather than adding a dead menu entry.

Added tests for the new timestamp formatter, the JWT email decoding, and the avatar/name header; updated existing drawer/composer tests for the new icon and format. Full suite (429 tests) and `flutter analyze` are clean.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/wagnerduarte/cerne/cfg-ciclo-a/skills/coletar-sessao

Você recebeu o argumento `<ID>`, onde `<ID>` é um de: `SETUP`, `PLAN`, `F000`, `RF01`…`RF10`.

**Se `<ID>` não foi fornecido, ou não é exatamente um desses valores: PARE. Não adivinhe, não infira pelo que estava sendo discutido na sessão. Pergunte ao usuário qual ID usar e espere a resposta antes de rodar qualquer coisa.** Gravar o ID errado corrompe a atribuição de tempo/tokens por unidade de trabalho (M1-M3) — é um erro sério, não um detalhe.

Rode exatamente este comando, pelo caminho absoluto (nunca relativo — esta skill roda de dentro do repositório do ciclo, não de `cerne-avaliacao`), substituindo `<ID>` pelo argumento recebido e `<CICLO>` por `a` ou `b` conforme o `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` desta sessão (`cfg-ciclo-a` → `a`; `cfg-ciclo-b` → `b`):

```
python3 /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-avaliacao/scripts/coletar_sessao.py skill <ID> --ciclo <CICLO> --versao-claude-code "$(claude --version)" --config-raciocinio "$CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL" --otel-output ~/cerne/otelcol/output.jsonl
```

Exiba ao usuário **exatamente e apenas** a saída do script, sem adicionar nada, sem resumir, sem comentar tokens/tempo/custo (o script nunca imprime isso, mas se por algum motivo a saída contiver algo parecido, não repita nem elabore sobre isso — é uma falha a reportar, não a esconder).

Depois de exibir a saída, a sessão está encerrada para fins de medição. Não envie nenhuma mensagem adicional, não ofereça ajuda, não pergunte nada — esta é a última ação da sessão.
